summary: Put related repository work inside one service transaction and understand proxy calls and managed entities.

A service method defines the boundary when several repository operations belong together.
Separate repository calls do not automatically form one shared service transaction.
Spring applies transaction handling through a proxy around the service bean.

The proxy opens or joins the transaction before calling the method.

example.title: Save two employees in one transaction
description: The tabs contain all application files for this separate Maven project.
The example requires Java 17 or later, Maven and PostgreSQL with an existing `employee_notes` database.
`database/schema.sql` creates the tables in an empty database before `mvn spring-boot:run`.
Hibernate validates the supplied schema. It does not create the tables.
Another Spring bean calls `createPair` through its injected `EmployeeBatchService`.
explanation: The proxy starts a transaction before either `save` runs.
Both repository calls join that transaction.
If a database write fails, a runtime exception normally causes rollback of both writes.
A successful method return allows the transaction manager to commit.

A persistence context tracks entity objects loaded or saved during a unit of JPA work.
A tracked object is called managed.
Hibernate checks its mapped fields for changes and can write those changes when the transaction flushes.
This tracking is called dirty checking.
